answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a jury-duty liability mechanism. Each new identity must serve as a juror for five epochs, with a penalty of 20 tokens for any voting divergence from the panel. This structure anchors legitimacy in genuine participation, as costs accumulate for every additional identity. An attacker creating ten identities could face penalties exceeding 200 tokens. Flooding the system becomes like trying to fill a hollow vessel with water through a shrinking inlet—eventually, it all spills out, making the effort unsustainable.
